items.title: Hubert Laws — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Gandhi says, “You have to become the change you want to see.”

ctx.x: Music has given me the opportunity to make many friends, many relationships. But those relationships, that doesn’t govern moral behavior. See, music can make you feel good in some ways. It can sort of corroborate what your sentiments are. But it cannot dictate moral behavior. You can have the same person in prison love your music. See, because they’ve violated some morality of government. You can still – you can be united in the fact you like the same pieces. That doesn’t have anything to do with your good or bad…

Okay, so divine influences, but we all – most of us who have been able to inculcate that discipline had strong models. Gandhi says, “You have to become the change you want to see.” Or, as a father, you have to model that behavior for your children. So a lot of that, maybe there is divine, but as human beings, we have the interpersonal relationships that we’re dealing with. I overheard – I remember hearing Dick Gregory say – he says, don’t have your kids lie for you, if somebody comes to the door and you tell them…
